text: Louisiana: lawyers must file their ads with a bar or court office, by the time the ad first runs. The standard fee is $175 per ad.
note: Fees are per separate/distinct advertisement or communication. New-lawyer discount: members admitted less than 3 years and not affiliated with a firm of 5+ lawyers pay $100 per timely filing, with an additional $100 late fee ($200 total), stated on the LSBA filing page as effective 11/11/2022. The rule text says fees are 'in an amount set by the Supreme Court of Louisiana'; no primary source found stating when the current $175/$275 amounts took effect. Re-filing after a change of circumstances requires 'an additional fee as set by the Court' (Rule 7.7(i)); amount not stated on the filing page. No expedited/rush review appears in the LSBA fee schedule (advisory, regular, late, new-lawyer only), so expedited_available is 'no'. Rules text read from LSBA PDF labelled 'With amendments through January 1, 2022'; the LSBA advertising home page still links rule history only through 2011 orders, and I did not find a later amending order, but confirm no post-2022 amendments to Rules 7.1-7.10. The Committee must complete review within 30 days or notify the lawyer; if no written communication within 30 days, the ad is deemed approved (Rule 7.7(e)).
